tutorial.title: Timeout and Intervals in JS
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn about the asynchronous methods in JavaScript: setTimeout, setInterval and clearInterval.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
JavaScript has some native methods that execute code asynchronously, such as setTimeout() and setInterval().

In this chapter, we'll take a look at the setTimeout() method.

lessons.title: setTimeout()
lessons.interactiveContent:
The setTimeout() method sets a timer, in milliseconds, that executes a function or code block when the timer expires.

Code your first setTimeout method in the example code.

Make sure to pick setTimeout.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The setTimeout() method sets a timer, in milliseconds, that executes a function or code block when the timer expires.

Schedule one callback only, so Executed Second prints before Executed Last.

Make sure to pick setTimeout, followed by =>.

lessons.title: setTimeout() 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
The code here is asynchronous. That means that while we wait for the callback to be executed, the code after the setTimeout method runs.

The console output from the setTimeout method will show last because of the delay in the setTimeout method.

Make sure to pick setTimeout.
lessons.hardModeContent:
While a timeout waits, code after the timer call continues to run.

Schedule the callback once with a delay twice as long as 1000 milliseconds.

Make sure to pick setTimeout, followed by 2000.

lessons.title: Delay Parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
The delay parameter is the time, in milliseconds, that passes before the function or code block executes.

In the following code, set a 2000 millisecond delay for the code block to execute.

Make sure to pick 2000.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The delay parameter is the time, in milliseconds, that passes before the function or code block executes.

Schedule Executed after 2 seconds once after two seconds while the final log continues immediately.

Make sure to pick setTimeout, followed by 2000.

lessons.title: Delay of 0
lessons.interactiveContent:
setTimeout() is always asynchronous, even if the delay parameter is omitted or we set it as 0.

With a delay of 0, the code after the setTimeout() method executes immediately, but the callback function is executed as soon as possible.

Make sure to pick 0.

lessons.title: Callback Function
lessons.interactiveContent:
setTimeout() executes the callback after the specified delay.

The code after the setTimeout continues to execute regardless of whether a callback or code block is used.

Make sure to pick callback.
lessons.hardModeContent:
setTimeout() executes the callback after the specified delay.

The code after the setTimeout continues to execute regardless of whether a callback or code block is used.

Pass the named function that prints Executed Last because of setTimeout after two seconds.

Make sure to pick callback.

lessons.title: Question: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
What statement is true regarding JavaScript methods?

JavaScript has some methods that execute code asynchronouslyJavaScript only has methods that execute code synchronously

JavaScript has some methods that execute code asynchronously.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A method schedules cleanup, then the next line prints Ready before cleanup runs. What explains this order?

Some JavaScript methods schedule work asynchronously while later code continuesEvery JavaScript method finishes all of its work before the next line runsScheduling cleanup pauses Ready until the callback finishes

Some JavaScript methods schedule work asynchronously while later code continues.

lessons.title: Question: setTimeout()
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the setTimeout() method do?

It executes a callback function when a timer expiresIt only sets a timer

It executes a callback function when a timer expires.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You run setTimeout(sendReport, 500). What happens to sendReport?

It runs after the 500-millisecond timer expiresThe timer expires without ever running sendReportIt runs immediately, and the timer starts after it finishes

It runs after the 500-millisecond timer expires.

lessons.title: Question: setTimeout() 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What statement is true regarding the setTimeout() method?

It is an asynchronous JavaScript methodIt is a synchronous JavaScript method

It is an asynchronous JavaScript method.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The code schedules showMessage with a delay of 0, then logs Next. What happens first?

Next is logged before showMessage runsshowMessage runs first because a zero delay makes the call synchronousBoth actions wait because setTimeout() blocks the current code

Next is logged before showMessage runs.

lessons.title: Question: Delay Parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the delay parameter of setTimeout() do?

It specifies how many milliseconds pass before the callback is executedIt causes all of the code to stop executing

It specifies how many milliseconds pass before the callback is executed.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A call uses setTimeout(updateStatus, 3000). What does 3000 control?

The timer waits 3000 milliseconds before updateStatus can runAll JavaScript stops for 3000 milliseconds before the next line can runupdateStatus repeats every 3000 milliseconds

The timer waits 3000 milliseconds before updateStatus can run.

lessons.title: Question: Delay of 0
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the default value of the delay parameter when we don't pass a value to it?

0 milliseconds1000 milliseconds

0 milliseconds.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The code calls setTimeout(showAlert) without a delay, then logs Done. How is the missing delay treated?

It defaults to 0 milliseconds, but showAlert still runs after current codeIt defaults to 1000 milliseconds before showAlert runsIt makes showAlert run synchronously before Done

It defaults to 0 milliseconds, but showAlert still runs after current code.

lessons.title: Question: Callback Function
lessons.interactiveContent:
When is the callback function of setTimeout() executed?

After the timer set by the delay parameter expiresBefore the timer set by the delay parameter expires

After the timer set by the delay parameter expires.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A two-second timer schedules loadPreview, and later lines keep running. When can loadPreview execute?

After its two-second timer expires, while the later lines were free to continueBefore its timer expires if the later lines finish earlyOnly after every other statement in the entire program has permanently stopped

After its two-second timer expires, while the later lines were free to continue.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
setInterval() is another native JavaScript method that executes code asynchronously.

With setInterval we can execute some code every set period of time. Let's learn more about this method.

lessons.title: setInterval()
lessons.interactiveContent:
setInterval() takes a callback function and an interval as parameters. Here, the toggleBlinker switches on and off the blinkers.

Pass the callback function and the interval to the setInterval call.

Make sure to pick setInterval, followed by toggleBlinker, and finally 500.
lessons.hardModeContent:
setInterval() takes a callback function and an interval as parameters. Here, toggleBlinker switches the blinkers.

Complete the arrow function and repeat toggleBlinker every 500 milliseconds.

Make sure to pick =>, followed by setInterval, toggleBlinker, and finally 500.

lessons.title: Interval
lessons.interactiveContent:
setInterval executes the callback function forever, with a delay of the specified number of milliseconds we pass as the second parameter.

The first execution of the callback occurs after the time specified. It doesn't execute immediately.

Make sure to pick 500.
lessons.hardModeContent:
setInterval executes the callback forever, with the delay in milliseconds passed as the second parameter.

The first execution of the callback occurs after the time specified. It doesn't execute immediately.

Run the blinker callback every half second, starting after the first half second.

Make sure to pick setInterval, followed by 500.

lessons.title: setInterval() Callback
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we run the code we might get a timeout error because there's no stop to the setInterval.

Add 500 milliseconds here to see the code go on and off forever every 500 milliseconds!

Make sure to type 500.

lessons.title: Stopping the Interval
lessons.interactiveContent:
To stop setInterval() from running indefinitely, we can use the clearInterval method.

We can save the setInterval in a blinkerInterval variable. Then use clearInterval(blinkerInterval) inside a setTimeout to be executed after 2500 milliseconds.

Make sure to pick let followed by blinkerInterval and then clearInterval, blinkerInterval, 2500.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The setInterval call returns a timer ID. Pass that ID to clearInterval to stop repeating.

Save the repeating timer in blinkerInterval.

After 2500 milliseconds, cancel that timer and then print STOP!.

Make sure to pick let, followed by blinkerInterval, setTimeout, clearInterval, blinkerInterval, and finally 2500.

lessons.title: intervalID/clearInterval()
lessons.interactiveContent:
The clearInterval() method takes the blinkerInterval as its sole parameter.

On execution, it stops the repeating action of the setInterval() method.

Make sure to pick clearInterval, followed by blinkerInterval.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The clearInterval() method takes the blinkerInterval as its sole parameter.

On execution, it stops the repeating action of the setInterval() method.

Use the delayed callback to cancel blinkerInterval before printing STOP!.

Make sure to pick setTimeout, followed by clearInterval, and finally blinkerInterval.

lessons.title: Question: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is a JavaScript method that executes code asynchronously?

setInterval().filter()

Make sure to pick setInterval().
lessons.hardModeContent:
A dashboard must call checkStatus every second without blocking later code. Which method fits?

setInterval().filter(), because it schedules each status check on a timersetTimeout(), because one timeout repeats until it is cleared

Make sure to pick setInterval().

lessons.title: Question: setInterval() Delay
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the delay parameter specify for the setInterval() method?

The number of milliseconds that'll pass between executions of the callbackThe number of minutes that'll pass between executions of the callback

The number of milliseconds that'll pass between executions of the callback.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The code runs setInterval(refreshWeather, 5000). What does 5000 mean?

About 5000 milliseconds pass between calls to refreshWeatherFive thousand minutes pass between calls to refreshWeatherOnly the first call waits 5000 milliseconds, then the interval stops

About 5000 milliseconds pass between calls to refreshWeather.

lessons.title: Question: Stopping the Interval
lessons.interactiveContent:
What statement is true regarding the setInterval() method?

It runs indefinitely unless we add additional code to stop itIt only allows the callback to execute 10 times

It runs indefinitely unless we add additional code to stop it.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The code runs setInterval(pingServer, 1000) and never clears its timer. What happens?

pingServer keeps running about once per second until code stops the intervalpingServer stops automatically after ten callspingServer runs once after one second, like a timeout

pingServer keeps running about once per second until code stops the interval.

lessons.title: Question: setInterval() Callback
lessons.interactiveContent:
What are two common parameters that setInterval() has?

A callback function and a delaysetInterval() only accepts a callback function as a parameter

A callback function and a delay.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In setInterval(updateClock, 1000), what do the two arguments represent?

updateClock is the callback, and 1000 is the delay between callsBoth arguments are callbacks that alternate every second1000 is passed into updateClock each time it runs

updateClock is the callback, and 1000 is the delay between calls.

lessons.title: Question: intervalID/clearInterval()
lessons.interactiveContent:
What method can we use to stop the execution of setInterval()?

clearInterval()setTimeout

Make sure to pick clearInterval().
lessons.hardModeContent:
JavaScript provides a method to stop a running setInterval() timer.

The variable pollingId stores a running interval. Which call stops that specific interval?

clearInterval(pollingId)setTimeout(pollingId)clearTimeout(pollingId), because every timer uses the timeout clearer

Make sure to pick clearInterval(pollingId).
